title: Flipp Tripp
status: Pre launch: review build waiting on the owner's confirmations; a requested new look has not started
seoTitle: Flipp Tripp: a split flap website case study
description: How I built a brand film studio's first website: a split flap board of verified facts, a launch gate on unconfirmed claims, and 42 of 42 checks passing.
deck: The studio had no showreel to lead with, so its first website leads with a split flap board of verified facts.
summary: Flipp Tripp, a brand film studio, had no website, no published email, phone number or address, and no showreel or film masters to design from. Its name also sits beside travel businesses.

I ran agent workflows for fact checked research and a design contest of three concepts, then built a site whose proof is its design: a split flap board of verified facts that settles once and waits. An adversarial review tested it the same day.

The launch build is gated. An indexable build fails while any owner confirmation is missing, people stay hidden until they consent, and the home page sets 0 cookies. 42 of 42 acceptance checks pass on the review build, and reach opens at launch.

offer.who: Founder led studios and small brands that need a first website but have little public proof yet, and open questions about rights, consent or who runs the business.
offer.gets: A brief researched from public records and standards, a design chosen from competing concepts, a site built to written speed and accessibility targets with one signature interaction, search basics with structured data and share images, privacy and terms text built only from confirmed facts, a launch gate, and one command that reruns the acceptance checks.
offer.needs: Your confirmations: who runs the business, an inbox and a domain, and a grievance contact. Written permission from each client you want to show, consent from anyone on screen, and your master files: logo, films and stills.
offer.setup: On this project, research, design, build and review all happened on one day, 12 Oct 2026. Launch then waits only on your confirmations; switching on is configuration and a rerun of the checks.

sources.text: Acceptance run of the project's own check script against the review build, reading the served pages with JavaScript off, 25 Oct 2026. All 42 checks passed: routes 4, SEO 9, structure and links 6, copy 17, served without JavaScript 3, privacy and leaks 3. Among them: the sitemap lists exactly the 7 published pages, the structured data carries the 6 types the script expects, and share images render for Home and the 4 case pages.

Home page load in headless Chromium 153 at 1440 by 900, unthrottled, with every request to another host aborted and counted; cookies and storage read 7 s after load. Run on 25 Oct 2026 IST (24 Oct 2026, 22:15 UTC). Result: 0 cookies, 0 local storage keys, 0 session storage keys and 0 third party requests attempted.

Same session. A MutationObserver timed every flap layer added inside the home board, whose 26 tiles each add two layers per flip. On load: 188 layers, so 94 flips, the first at 1,324.8 ms and the last at 2,255.9 ms after navigation start, still 1.04 s after the first flap; then 0 layers in the next 6.06 s with no input. One click with no pointer movement: 38 layers, the first new flap at 46.1 ms and the last at 512.3 ms, still at 622 ms. Still time is the last layer plus one 110 ms step. With reduced motion emulated: 0 layers on load and on press, and the row text swapped at once. One unthrottled lab session, not field data.

The project's adversarial review, 12 Oct 2026. Five lenses (bugs, accessibility, visual craft, performance and SEO, claims) proposed 44 findings; a second pass checked each one, mostly by reproducing it in a browser, and confirmed 33, rejecting 11 as behaviour the spec intended. Confirmed by severity: 3 blocker, 7 major, 23 minor. All 33 were fixed that day, as the project's optimisation record notes. The four findings described on this page are bugs 1 and 7 and accessibility 1 and 3. Counted on 25 Oct 2026.

The client's flap engine, board component and tile styles, read 25 Oct 2026. The engine: 128 lines by wc, 110 ms a tile step, a pool of 37 glyphs (A to Z, 0 to 9 and &), one time ordered queue on one requestAnimationFrame loop that stops when the queue is empty. The board: the settle runs 2 to 4 random glyphs a tile, 35 ms apart by column and 120 ms by row, and a blank tile runs one random glyph; a press flips changed tiles only, through one random glyph and then the target, 35 ms apart by column. The styles: the fold and landing layers, each half a step long, with a shade on the moving leaf.

The project's build spec, written from the design contest on 12 Oct 2026: the shade rising from 0 to 0.45 as a leaf folds (line 304); every board still within 1.2 s and a press within 0.65 s (lines 169 and 306); the offline enquiry mode and the steps for switching on (928 to 955); legal text gated by confirmation (957 to 979); and SEO, with 6 structured data types, 5 share images and a sitemap of 7 pages (1053 to 1121). The copy pass that removed five unverified marketing lines is in lines 765 to 770. Read 25 Oct 2026.

The project's research brief, 12 Oct 2026: five research tracks and three follow up passes with fact check verdicts (line 3); the brand's public footprint (57 to 58 and 158); 15 standards and legal sources (108 to 124), among them WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.2.2, which asks for a pause control when automatic motion lasts more than 5 s, and Copyright Act section 17(b); 11 items never to state as fact (126 to 137); the rule that no content item is published without the owner's confirmation of rights (178); 16 firm content items and 11 possible ones (180 to 215); the cookie plan, no banner at launch and a fresh check before 13 May 2027 (118 and 569 to 573); 16 owner questions and 16 risks (662 to 702). Read 25 Oct 2026.

The project's own notes, read 25 Oct 2026: the decisions log (a research workflow of 17 agents with every track fact checked; the design contest; the owner's request of 23 Oct 2026), the progress log for 12 Oct 2026 (built on the Post Aura scaffold, five builder agents in parallel, 42 of 42 checks green locally and on the review build, review fixes deployed) and the mistakes and lessons log.

The client's source code, read 25 Oct 2026: the launch gate in the root layout; the confirmation flags and the list of what is missing in the legal settings, with email delivery live only when the operator and three settings exist; 4 people stored with consent set to false, and the credit filter that runs on the server, in the work registry; 2 held cases in a file that nothing imports; and the site settings, where only a real domain makes a build indexable.

The design contest results, 12 Oct 2026: three concepts scored by design, brand and engineering judge agents. Departures 8, 8.1 and 8.5; The Keynote Cut 7, 7 and 7; The Flip Side 6.5, 6.5 and 5.5. Across the three verdicts, 49 must fix items and 37 grafts, some overlapping. The design judge's note on the first build: its hero cycled forever behind a pause button, at about nine flips a second per tile across 26 tiles. Read 25 Oct 2026.

The client repository, read 25 Oct 2026: its package file (four runtime dependencies, Next.js, React, React DOM and motion, and one check command that builds the site and runs the acceptance script); the acceptance script's header (its rule, line 20); the optimisation record (20 static routes in the production build, checks green before and after); and the git reflog, where commits 9bb04ab, 0031073 and 2458c5a landed at 09:36, 10:29 and 11:57 IST on 12 Oct 2026.

stage.heading: How one flap turns
stage.intro: Every tile on the studio's board is modelled on a physical flap. Step through one change by hand, then type your own words onto a board that keeps the same timing. I wrote this board fresh for this page; it is not the client's code.

cut.heading: Step through one flip

example.text: Example flip: F to T, through one random glyph, 7.

slider.label: Step through one flip

help.text: Each step is 110 ms: the old leaf folds for 55 ms, then the new one lands for 55 ms. This example takes two steps, F to 7, then 7 to T.

slider.noJs: Turn on JavaScript to step through the flip.

cut.loadError: The controls did not load. The steps below describe the flip in full.

valueText.fold: {t} milliseconds, step {step} of 2: the old top leaf is falling.
valueText.edge: {t} milliseconds, step {step} of 2: both leaves edge on, {next} above, {prev} below.
valueText.land: {t} milliseconds, step {step} of 2: the new bottom leaf is landing.

steps.text: At rest a tile shows two halves of one glyph. When it changes, the top half behind the old leaf already holds the next glyph.
The old top leaf folds down about its bottom edge, darkening as it turns. At 55 ms it stands edge on and disappears.
The new bottom leaf unfolds from edge on and lands over the old bottom half as its shade lifts. One step takes 110 ms.
A press runs each changed tile through one random glyph from a pool of 37, then the new letter: two steps. The first settle runs two to four random glyphs before each letter.

lede.text: The studio had no website. None of its public channels gave an email address, a phone number or a postal address, and its only active channel was Instagram.

parts.text: There was no showreel, no logo master, no colour file and no set of film masters. The only logo was a small social media avatar. Searching the name returned mostly namesakes, including travel businesses that hold similar trademarks.

At the start I launched a research workflow of 17 agents, alongside the first build: five tracks and three follow up passes, each with fact check verdicts. The brief states as fact only what the fact check agents verified or two registries agreed on.

It mapped the legal ground early. Under Indian copyright law, a film made for payment belongs first to the client who commissioned it unless they agree otherwise, so every commissioned film needed its client's written permission. The business behind the brand was checked against public registries, and no legal page names an operator until the owner confirms who runs it.
It also found that Apple's SF Pro licence forbids use on websites, so the site sets Inter with optical sizes, at type values read from apple.com's own stylesheets.

cannot-say-too-much.label: EVERY BUILD
cannot-say-too-much.heading: A site that cannot say too much

lede.text: A launch build may state only what has been confirmed, and the code enforces it.

parts.text: The launch gate

Only a real domain makes a build indexable. If an indexable build starts while any owner confirmation is missing, it fails with an error that lists each one, including the operator, the grievance officer, live email delivery, every client's written permission and the launch date. Review builds stay out of search.
Launch gate: operator not confirmed; grievance officer not named; enquiry email delivery not live; no permission from a client; launch date for Privacy and Terms not set.
parts.caption: The gate's error message, recreated with names removed and the list shortened.

parts.text: Legal text from confirmed facts

Privacy and Terms are generated from configuration. The operator, the grievance officer, the courts and the liability clauses render only once confirmed, and a draft note says so until then. Confirming a fact switches its sentence on across every page in the next build.
Names behind consent

People are stored with a consent flag, and credits are filtered on the server, so an unconsented name never reaches a page or a browser bundle. Held cases live in a file that nothing imports, and their addresses return 404. The checks scan every served byte and every bundle for leaks.

items.label: stored in the code, shown on no page until they consent.
kept in a file that nothing imports.

parts.text: An honest offline form

Until the operator, the inbox and email delivery are confirmed, Send is disabled and a note points visitors to Instagram. If the server is reached anyway, it stores nothing and answers with the same note. In offline mode, success is never faked.
Privacy without a banner

Films load only on a press, through Vimeo's do not track mode and YouTube's privacy enhanced domain. Fonts are self hosted, no cookie is set and nothing is stored, so the research brief plans no consent banner at launch, with a fresh check due before India's new data protection duties start on 13 May 2027. The Privacy Policy describes what the build does, and the stage above shows the measurement.

parts.text: Search engines and AI assistants get the same facts as structured data: the organisation, the site, its pages, each case, one film and the breadcrumbs, and never Person, Review or AggregateRating. An llms.txt file says plainly that the studio is not a travel agency.

The name sits beside travel businesses, so the site speaks in film words. The winning concept gave up its name, Departures, and became The Board. The 404 page reads “This frame didn’t make the cut.” A check fails on any travel word outside a short allowlist.

parts.text: The contest

Three concepts went to three judge agents, one lens each: design, brand and engineering. Between them the judges wrote 49 must fix items, some overlapping, and 37 grafts. The spec took every must fix item and a selection of the grafts: the press that turns STORIES FIRST into YOUR STORY FIRST came from The Keynote Cut, the Show all credits view from The Flip Side.

parts.caption: Scores from three judge agents, 12 Oct 2026.

parts.text: The spec build answered them. One shared animation clock replaced per tile React state and timers, every board settles once and then waits, and the travel labels gave way to film words.
The review

Five review lenses proposed 44 findings. A second pass then checked each one, mostly by reproducing it in a browser: 33 held up, and 11 were rejected as behaviour the spec intended. All 33 were fixed the same day: 3 blockers, 7 major and 23 minor. Four of them taught me how the parts work.

items.what: Only the first flap of each tile animated.
items.cause: Each step's cleanup came due at the same instant as the next step, so it erased that step's layers.
items.fix: A cleanup now checks that it still owns its layer.

items.what: The one animation loop multiplied: 2,483 frame requests over 96 frames, up to 50 in a single frame, across three presses.
items.cause: The loop cleared its own flag before running jobs, so any job that scheduled work started a second loop.
items.fix: The flag stays set while jobs run, and a failing job cannot stall the clock.

items.what: Board labels stayed blank on phones.
items.cause: Their settle waited for 25% of the board to be visible. Opened in full, the board grew to 4,005 px, and an 844 px screen can show at most 21% of it.
items.fix: The settle now starts from the board's top edge.

items.what: In page links scrolled but left keyboard focus behind.
items.cause: The new scroll handler in Next.js 16.3 leaves focus where it was, by design.
items.fix: Same page links became plain anchors, so the next Tab starts where the page scrolled to.

lede.text: The build needs only the owner's confirmations to launch; the requested new look has not started.

sum.text: 5 steps. Three for the owner, two for me.

steps.action: Confirm what the gate lists, among them the operating entity, a grievance contact, each client's written permission and the launch date.
Name the inbox for enquiries and agree to an email delivery provider, which needs the site's domain verified.
Add three empty email settings to the project and its host.
Paste the values in. Nobody echoes them back.
Set the site's domain, switch the confirmed flags on, rebuild, and run the 42 checks against it.

parts.back: each confirmation is one setting. Set it back and its sentence leaves every page at the next build, and without the operator or any email setting, the form returns to offline mode.

parts.text: The contract

One command builds the site, serves it and runs 42 checks against the served pages with JavaScript off, and the same script runs against any address. Its rule sits at the top of the file: change it when the spec changes, never to make a failure pass.

parts.caption: The 42 checks by group, run against the review build on 25 Oct 2026.

parts.text: Small on purpose
The flap engine is 128 lines of TypeScript. The site runs on four runtime dependencies and builds to 20 static routes.
What I learned

Tracing the board frame by frame taught me that a timer can outlive the step that set it. The focus bug taught me to read a framework's defaults before trusting them. And with thin public proof, trust has to come from exact credits and rules that refuse a guess, never from scale.
